answer_1.quote: We study this question—fingerspelling within sign language translation—in the context of translation from American Sign Language to English, trained on a noisy ∼2800‑hour superset of YouTube‑ASL and evaluated on FLEURS‑ASL.
answer_1.outputs: English text translations of ASL video clips

answer_2.quote: We find that 1) provides substantial improvements in overall translation quality; more of this gain comes from sentences with fingerspelling (37.3 → 44.8 BLEURT) ... and the accuracy of fingerspelled phrases within those translations improves dramatically (76.6% CER → 41.6% CER).

answer_3.quote: We automatically identify the relevant spans with an LLM. ... We use an LLM, Gemini 1.5 Pro, as the annotator rather than humans; see Figure for a summary.
methods: LLM prompt for span extraction of fingerspelled terms
